Pastor Rotimi Okpaise has emerged as a central figure in the leadership crisis at The Fountain of Life Church, Lagos, after a group identifying itself as the church’s Board of Trustees appointed him interim spiritual and administrative leader. The appointment, announced on Tuesday, followed the group’s decision to withdraw recognition of Pastor Jimmy Odukoya as Senior Pastor, a move Odukoya and the church have rejected. The trustees said Okpaise would oversee the church’s spiritual and administrative affairs pending consultations and the establishment of a substantive leadership structure. Here are five things to know about Okpaise and the circumstances surrounding his appointment. 1. He was named interim spiritual and administrative leader The group of trustees announced Okpaise’s appointment in a statement issued on Tuesday, November 17, after reaffirming its November 16 resolution withdrawing recognition of Jimmy Odukoya as Senior Pastor. The trustees said the interim arrangement would remain in place while they consulted and undertook other processes to establish a substantive leadership structure in line with the church’s governing instruments. The board stated, “The Board has further resolved that the interim spiritual and administrative leadership of the Church be entrusted to Pastor Rotimi Okpaise.” The appointment came amid competing claims over who has the authority to determine the church’s leadership. 2. According to his professional profile published by CrusaderSterling Pensions, he retired from Ernst & Young, where he served as a partner and led the insurance sector and actuarial services practice across West Africa. He also served as statutory actuary to several leading insurance companies in the region. 3. Qualifications Okpaise is a Fellow of the Institute of Actuaries in the United Kingdom and an Associate of the Society of Actuaries in the United States. His professional experience also includes serving as reporting actuary to four Contributory Pension Fund Administrators and the pension schemes of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company and the National Pension Commission. These roles formed part of his career in the financial and insurance sectors before his retirement from Ernst & Young. Education background Okpaise holds a degree in Statistics from the University of Ibadan, where he was recognised as a University Scholar. He also attended the Lagos Business School’s Chief Executive Programme. His academic and professional qualifications combine a background in statistics, actuarial practice and executive management. 5. Instrumental in Jimmy Odukoya’s appointment According to Church Gist, Okpaise previously played a prominent role in the church’s leadership transition following the death of Taiwo Odukoya in August 2023. On September 17, 2023, he announced to the congregation that the Board of Trustees had unanimously chosen Jimmy Odukoya to succeed his father as Senior Pastor. Jimmy’s sister, Pastor Tolu Odukoya-Ijogun, was also announced as Associate Senior Pastor. The development has become a notable part of the current dispute, given that Okpaise, who announced Jimmy’s emergence, has now been named to oversee the church on an interim basis by the group of trustees seeking his removal. The controversy surrounding Okpaise’s appointment followed a dispute over the succession arrangements left by the church’s late founder, Taiwo Odukoya. In its November 17 statement, the group of trustees said it had reviewed a video recording allegedly made in December 2021, in which the late founder identified Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor in the event of his death or incapacitation. According to the trustees, the recording indicated that Jimmy was expected to serve as Areogun’s administrative assistant and lead the youth church. They alleged that the video was not presented to the board when Jimmy’s appointment was considered in 2023, and said its disclosure could have influenced the decision. The trustees also cited governance and doctrinal concerns, including issues surrounding Jimmy’s remarriage, as part of the reasons for their intervention. However, Jimmy rejected the announcement of his removal, insisting that he remained the duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees. A statement published in the church’s name described the purported removal as constitutionally invalid and argued that the individuals behind it were acting outside the church’s governing framework. It also claimed that some trustees had been asked to resign in March 2026 over alleged constitutional violations. The dispute escalated further after the trustees accused individuals acting on Jimmy’s behalf of taking control of the church’s official social media accounts without their authorisation. They warned that statements published on the platforms should not be regarded as the board’s official position unless authorised by the trustees. The competing statements have left the church facing uncertainty over its leadership, the authority of its trustees and the succession arrangements established by its late founder.
